- An ex-Ford designer envisions the Roamer sharing its underpinnings with the R1S and R1T.
- The design includes rear doors and C-pillars with built-in ladders for easy rooftop access.
- Unfortunately, Rivian has given no indication that it’s developing a model like this.
Whereas most EV startups have attempted to penetrate the market with either mass-market models or high-end hypercars, Rivian went about things differently with the R1S and R1T. The two models, based around the same skateboard architecture, are focused on adventurers who want to enjoy the wilderness and all the practicality that a vehicle focused on this area offers.
Inspired by the R1T and R1S, former Ford and Pininfarina designer Aditya Narayan has imagined what could be the ultimate Rivian adventure vehicle. It’s dubbed the Roamer, and whereas the R1T is a pickup and the R1S is an SUV, the Roamer is an eye-catching van similar in size to its siblings and designed to tackle the most treacherous terrain imaginable.
Read: Rivian Is Cutting Costs But Still Loses Over $32,000 On Every EV It Builds
From a visual standpoint, the Roamer shares plenty in common with the R1 models. The front end features Rivian’s characteristic oval-shaped headlights, connected with an intricate light bar made up of dozens of little LEDs. One of the most interesting aspects of the car’s design is that the windshield stretches all the way to the headlights, meaning there’s no traditional hood. The front overhang is also very short.
The most intriguing design detail is found on the sides of the Roamer. Located on the rear doors and the thick C-pillars are five large cut-outs you can slide your feet into and use as a ladder. This would be very handy for a car like the Roamer as it’s equipped with a large rooftop tent, and the ladder provides easy access to it. Like the front, the rear is familiar Rivian, although the light bar of R1 and R2 models is now made up of dozens of little LEDs.
While we’d love to see Rivian build a van like this, it hasn’t publicized any plans to do so. The firm recently launched refreshed R1T and R1S models and is working on its cheaper, mass-market offerings, the R2 and R3.

documents.title: Shifting Gears : New Rivian R1 vehicles have  hundred of design , engineering , performance changes
Unofficial Rivian Roamer Design Project Becomes Even More Enticing With  Roamcube  Trailer
documents.text:
Sure, it's going to take them a long time toward sustainable growth before they can brag about offering the best-selling vehicle in the world, as Tesla did last year with the Model Y crossover. The good thing is they didn't set on a conflicting path with either Tesla or Lucid like Fisker did with the Ocean crossover SUV – and now they're reaping the benefits of having both an off-road-focused pickup and an adventurous SUV on offer.
They also want to grow tremendously when they introduce the R2 and R3 models alongside the refreshed R1 series. Those will include smaller and cheaper models, but the characteristics will remain the same – power, performance, and style, all wrapped in an adventurous look. For sure, you can easily imagine the R1T, R1S, R2, R3, and R3X embarking on an overlanding adventure through a remote trail, more so than you would see them as mall crawlers, right?
Anyway, while we wait to see what happens with the recent $5 billion investment from Volkswagen and find out if the management can stop the cash bleed (Rivian announced mixed financial results for the second quarter of the year, and it's losing $33k per every vehicle it produces), it's maybe time to explore what could come next from the Irvine, California-based EV automaker.
If you listen to the parallel universes of vehicular CGI, then the imaginative realm of digital car content creators has a solution already. Cue to Aditya Narayan, the virtual artist better known as aditya__narayan on social media, who recently cooked up a cool new Rivian design project - it's completely unofficial but also mind-blowingly simple.
Using the R1 skateboard architecture, the pixel master envisioned a third large product for the company – the Rivian Roamer, a potentially ultimate all-electric overlanding minivan that could easily conquer any terrain in fantasy land. It's easy to recognize it as a true Rivian if you're a fan, given the quirky LED headlights or the clever integration of form and function, like the embedded steps that grant access to the pop-up roof tent, and it's too bad it's merely unofficial.
Well, the CGI expert has even more ideas – just recently he added to the design project the Rivian 'Roamcube' trailer, a place "for all those essentials you will never use." The design of the little trailer is expertly integrated and even comes with its own branding – the idea could take flight even on its own if it ever reaches the real world, frankly. So, what do you think?

documents.title: Rivian stops making electric vans for Amazon due to parts shortage
documents.text:
Rivian $RIVN has paused production of its electric van, which it built for Amazon $AMZN, because of a parts shortage. It’s the latest supply chain issue for the nascent EV maker.
Part shortages are common in the industry, a Rivian (RIVN) spokesperson told Bloomberg, adding that production of R1 electric pickup and SUV models is unaffected. All affected employees have the opportunity to continue working 40 hours a week during the pause.
The interruption marks another production hiccup for the EV maker as it works toward boosting output of its EV lineup next year. Irvine, California-based Rivian (RIVN) currently makes battery-electric SUVs and pickups at its Illinois factory, along with the delivery van that it supplies primarily to Amazon (AMZN), its biggest shareholder.
Rivian has amassed a surplus of the delivery vans at the plant that are awaiting delivery to Amazon (AMZN). The carmaker has a deal to supply the company with 100,000 vans by the end of the decade, and about 15,000 are already in service in the US.
A spokesperson for Amazon told Bloomberg it is aware of the issue Rivian is having, but it doesn’t expect to be impacted by it.
Rivian’s vans account for a fraction of the overall fleet used to deliver packages for Amazon, which taps gig workers who drive their own vehicles, as well as traditional couriers such as UPS (UPS) Corp.
Rivian Chief Financial Officer Claire McDonough has said the carmaker expects Amazon to take fewer deliveries during the fourth quarter, consistent with the online merchant’s seasonal pattern when it focuses on the holiday sales rush.
Earlier this month, Rivian doubled down on its target to build around 57,000 EVs this year between the van, the R1s SUV and the R1T pickup truck. That’s right in line with its 2023 levels.

documents.title: Why Rivian Stock Sank Friday , and Why Investors Shouldnt Panic
documents.text:
Rivian Automotive (NASDAQ: RIVN) shares were dropping on Friday afternoon after the company made a surprising announcement. While most of the focus on the electric vehicle (EV) maker has recently related to the unveiling of its next-generation SUV, today's news was about its commercial delivery vans.
Shares plunged as much as 5.5% on news that the company has suspended production of the vans destined for e-commerce giant Amazon. While the stock clawed back some of that drop, it was still trading lower by 4.3% as of 2:30 p.m. ET.
Rivian's massive EV order
Amazon placed a standing order for 100,000 electric delivery vans from Rivian to be delivered through the end of the decade. As of late last year, Amazon said it already had 10,000 Rivian vans in its delivery fleet. And Amazon isn't just a customer for Rivian. As an early investor, Amazon holds nearly 160 million shares, representing more than 16% ownership in Rivian as of April 29.
But today Rivian announced it was forced to temporarily suspend production of the electric Amazon vans due to a shortage of parts. The company didn't note what specific part or supplier was involved with the production halt. A Rivian spokesperson released an email statement saying, "A part shortage has temporarily impacted our Electric Delivery Van (EDV) production. We expect to recover all missed production."
Sales to Amazon represented about 19% of revenue for Rivian in 2023. But Rivian said production of its consumer pickup truck and SUV are not affected by the part shortage. For investors, this news is ultimately a non-issue. For those considering buying shares, it could, in fact, be an opportunity to get a slightly discounted share price.

documents.title: Rivian Camp Kitchen Is Officially Dead , Long Live the ( Pricey ) Travel Kitchen
documents.text:
Back in 2021, Rivian discreetly launched the R1T camp kitchen. It was made to fit perfectly in the gear tunnel and slide out of it effortlessly. Granted, it was expensive. It had a cost of about $5,000. However, that design included an induction cooktop, a collapsable sink, a water reservoir, three drawers, a 30-piece kitchen kit, and a coffee grinder. Imagine waking up in the Alabama Hills, California, and making fresh coffee while admiring the sunrise. That's quite the treat!
Sadly, the enthusiasm wore off pretty quickly because the young automaker wasn't delivering it. In late 2022, we learned that the camp kitchen was going to be discontinued. Four months later, it was nowhere to be found. Bummer all around.
However, Rivian customers were still willing to pay for an unofficial camp kitchen. In mid-2023, an 80-lb assembly made from plywood with a two-year warranty popped up unexpectedly. It didn't have a water tank, but it could be connected to an external one. It cost about $4,000, and many R1T owners ordered it. The company was so surprised by the positive feedback that it even decided to make one for the R1S.
Now, Rivian has officially buried that cool product and unearthed a new one—the "Travel Kitchen." Thanks to the R2, R3, and R3X tours, a prototype has already been shown around the US, which is how we could tell you about it before the official launch.
But now, the 41-lb Travel Kitchen is officially here, and it's not much to look at. It costs $1,400 and comes with a two-burner induction cooktop (up to 1,500 W), a surface to cut your veggies, a light strap, and a bit of storage space. It folds nicely into a cute 26.4-inch rectangle and can be stored in a special case with handles. Rivian offers a two-year warranty for it.
We can't blame Rivian for discontinuing the OG camp kitchen. It was very expensive and could have become a nightmare to fix or replace. However, this one is priced quite courageously and doesn't come at a good time. Recently, the brand announced Connect+, which is its version of Tesla's Premium Connectivity but $50 more expensive for a yearly subscription. Apart from being a bit pricey, there's nothing wrong with that. Rivian needs to become profitable, and it won't make shareholders any money by paying for its customers' mobile internet connection and other premium features.
At the end of the day, this product is most likely to disappoint existing and future R1T owners who wanted a cool slide-out kitchen for their pickup trucks' gear tunnels. There's a silver lining, though: it works for both R1T and R1S. Soon enough, it'll also be a good fit for the R2 and maybe even the R3 EVs!
Easy to carry, quick to set up, and perfect for bringing people together — we designed our new Travel Kitchen to make it simple to cook anything from snacks to unforgettable meals on the back of an R1T, an R1S or anywhere else your adventures take you. Available now:… pic.twitter.com/8biaZOjnjR
— Rivian (@Rivian) August 15, 2024

How Rivian Can Not Only Survive but Thrive Before the R2 Hits Roads
documents.text:
Long-term Rivian (RIVN +0.48%) investors might be experiencing some angst. The stock is down 85% since its late-2021 IPO. But while the electric vehicle (EV) industry trudges along with slower-than-anticipated growth, it's still rapidly evolving with cost cuts, vehicle launches, and improved battery technology, among other developments.
The question facing Rivian investors is, how does the company bridge the gap between now and what seems like an eternity before the R2 Rivian SUV launches its next growth phase? The answer for investors is hopefully something many have forgotten all about.
Remember electric delivery vans?
With all the developments surrounding Rivian and its path toward the R2, R3, and R3X, investors can be forgiven for forgetting all about the company's first big win: Its agreement with Amazon to deliver 100,000 electric delivery vans (EDVs) by 2030. Over the past nine months, Amazon has increased its U.S. EDV fleet by 50%, to 15,000 delivery vans. But that's not the current selling point for Rivian investors.
The current selling point is that the agreement with Amazon is no longer exclusive, which isn't new news. However, since the agreement went non-exclusive, the only major customer to sign on to start accepting deliveries of EDVs from Rivian has been AT&T. There was no wave of major customers beating down Rivian's door the moment the agreement went non-exclusive. So what's the deal?
Management noted a few quarters ago that the process for this doesn't happen overnight. Companies need to assess the viability of an electrified fleet saving costs and improving efficiency through data collection and reduced maintenance costs. They also have to test if it will have enough charging infrastructure and other capabilities to make the move a successful return on investment.
These pilot programs take time, and management noted that it would probably take a year of company testing before Rivian started inking more large deals similar to the one with Amazon. Investors could see some of these deals hopefully inked sometime in 2025, the seemingly uneventful year between the R1 refresh completed earlier this summer and the R2 launch during the first half of 2026.
Already, Rivian has 300 EDVs on the road in Germany, which could help spur additional overseas orders, in addition to the primary U.S. market.
NASDAQ: RIVN
Key Data Points
Better economics
It's also likely that investors will reap the benefits of Rivian ramping up to fulfill Amazon's original and ambitious order. Years ago, Amazon pledged to buy 100,000 EDVs by 2030. It took Rivian a year to deliver the first 5,000 units, followed by a four-month period to deliver another 5,000 units, and then nine additional months to deliver the next 5,000 units. Management still says it's on track to deliver its commitment and plans to ramp up larger fleet deployments such as Amazon's ahead of small-scale deployments starting in 2025.
Speaking of increased production and improved efficiency, Rivian plant retooling generated a 35% reduction in the cost of materials for vans and pushed the rate of assembly on the manufacturing line up roughly 30%. Rivian said earlier this summer that its overall cost across all lines has improved dramatically through removing over 100 steps in the battery-making process, 52 pieces of equipment from the body shop, and over 500 parts from the designs of its vehicles.
As Rivian continues to improve its production efficiency, reduce costs, and introduce more customers to its EDVs, it could be lighting the spark the company and investors need in 2025.

Prediction : Rivian and Lucid Will Succeed Where Fisker Failed
documents.text:
Electric vehicle (EV) maker Fisker served a stark reminder to investors that not all start-up EV companies will survive the early innings of this long-term transition in the automotive industry. Fisker had many problems including vehicle issues, poor management, and production hiccups. Most of all, the company's operations failed to lure in major backers and investors -- a problem Rivian (RIVN +0.48%) and Lucid (LCID +3.52%) currently don't have.
A German helping hand for Rivian
When a young automaker could use a helping hand developing EV technology and funding operations, few options are better than Volkswagen (VWAGY -2.60%), one of the largest automakers on the planet by production volume.
That's exactly what happened when Volkswagen agreed to invest up to $5 billion in Rivian to create an equally controlled joint venture to share and develop EV architecture and software, which initially sent shares of Rivian roughly 50% higher.
This investment will come in stages, with Volkswagen immediately investing $1 billion in Rivian through a note that will convert to stock on Dec. 1. Then, following that initial investment, Volkswagen will make a $1 billion payment at the inception of the joint venture later this year, and will invest another $1 billion in Rivian stock inn2025 and 2026, while also providing a $1 billion loan in 2026.
But this investment is about more than just the dollars Rivian is bringing in, although that certainly helps push its cash runway out to the launch of its R2 crossover, as well as the following R3 and R3X. The German investment will also help Rivian cut costs by leveraging larger volumes of key supplies including chips and other components, which will be instrumental in Rivian generating positive gross profits during the fourth quarter.
Perhaps most importantly, and also largely overlooked by investors, is that this partnership could lead Rivian's introduction into Europe and eventually Asia. Don't forget that Rivian already has a few hundred electric delivery vans operating in Germany. Volkswagen also benefits as the company has struggled to develop software on the level of Rivian, a competitive edge that Rivian hopes it can grow in the years ahead.
NASDAQ: RIVN
Key Data Points
Rivian wasn't the only start-up EV maker doing well enough to attract major investors. Lucid continues to prove its relationship with Saudi Arabia's backing is strong.
Enter the PIF for Lucid
Lucid has found out what many young automakers learn: Developing vehicles is challenging, expensive, and the industry has many outside variables not under the control of management. But what Lucid has also found, and what Fisker didn't, is deep pockets from an oil-rich country looking to hedge its future with electric vehicles.
Lucid announced in early August that an affiliate of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) will provide another cash infusion of up to $1.5 billion, which should keep the young EV maker funded into the fourth quarter of 2025 at least.
The backing of the PIF -- which invested a separate $1 billion as recently as March -- is absolutely critical for Lucid despite its compelling and well-designed Air sedan, because the company continues to burn through hundreds of millions of dollars quarterly to cover massive operating costs and a low volume of deliveries. Over the past several years the PIF has invested roughly $8 billion and owns a 60% stake in the young EV maker.
The hope is that PIF's seemingly endless backing and financial support will enable Lucid to deliver not only its upcoming Gravity electric SUV -- which the young EV maker believes will bring in a much larger consumer base -- but also its third model that will be a mid-size electric SUV. The SUV could be named Lucid Earth, based on trademarks filed by the automaker, with a price target of around $50,000 -- more affordable than the Air sedan, which can reach price tags well over $200,000.
Fisker's failure
Fisker shuttered its doors and filed for bankruptcy protection because the company's operations ultimately failed to convince major investors or other automakers to support its business vision. Thankfully for long-term investors of Rivian and Lucid, both young start-up EV makers have proven to large entities their future has merit and a chance to ride the automotive industry's EV transformation for years to come. That's why Rivian and Lucid will succeed where Fisker failed.

documents.title: GMC Confident Sierra EV Will Outsell Cybertruck , Ford , Rivian , And Others
documents.text:
- GMC believes it will overtake rivals to become the segment leader of the EV pickup truck space.
- The new Sierra EV is expected to outsell its Chevy Silverado EV counterpart and the Tesla Cybertruck.
- GMC plans to introduce more affordable models of the Sierra EV and Denali editions shortly.
While other manufacturers appear to be reneging on their EV plans, GMC apparently wants to continue its charge, as the company aims to become the leader for all-electric truck sales in the US. That’s according to Duncan Aldred, global vice president of GMC, who anticipates the new Sierra EV will win out against competition from Ford, Tesla, and Rivian.
The GMC Sierra EV is only just being rolled out to customers, with its rivals – including its sibling, the Chevrolet Silverado EV – having had a considerable headstart already. But, in the case of its Chevy stablemate, GMC is counting on the Sierra’s premium positioning as enough to differentiate it.
Read: 2024 GMC Sierra EV Gets More Range And $7.5k Lower Price
The GMC Sierra EV has plusher materials and larger screen real estate, while some of the more advanced features, such as Super Cruise and crab mode, are included as standard. However, both the Silverado and Sierra EVs have the same EPA-rated ranges of 440 miles (708 km), as well as the same power outputs, with up to 753 hp and 785 lb-ft of torque on offer.
Aside from competition within GM, there’s also the threat of the second-quarter sales star: the Tesla Cybertruck. However, despite the two being similarly priced, GMC isn’t anticipating that buyers will struggle to choose between the Cybertruck and the Sierra EV.
Speaking to CNBC, Aldred says that internal data indicates 70 percent of Cybertruck orders are from existing Tesla owners. Conversely, around 80 percent of Sierra EV reservation holders are non-GMC owners, meaning that the EV truck is attracting a new clientele to the brand.
GMC hasn’t said when they expect to become market leaders but they anticipate that sales will increase with lower-priced models of the Sierra EV, which will be introduced soon. However, the market for EVs has slowed down considerably, with Ford going so far as to delay its next EV truck entry from a planned production date of 2025 to 2027. Meanwhile, GMC’s own Hummer EV pickup has been slow to pick up in sales.

documents.title: Over 50 Rivian EVs Destroyed by Fire Outside of Factory
documents.text:
Over 50 Rivian vehicles were destroyed in a fire that broke out Saturday night at the electric vehicle company's factory in Normal, Illinois, according to photos from the scene and a local news report. No injuries were reported in the fire.
Witnesses reported seeing fire outside the Rivian factory shortly before 10 p.m. on Saturday night. The Normal Fire Department (NFD) responded and fought the blaze which was in a parking lot outside of the factory. NFD spokesperson Matt Swaney said that the fire was out by midnight on Sunday and that the EV factory was not damaged, according to 25 News Now.
There has been no official word on the number of vehicles damaged in the fire. However, aerial photos and video posted to a Rivian Facebook group show that about 50 to 60 vehicles were torched and appear to be a total loss. The damaged vehicles were cordoned off by box cars and barriers in the corner of the parking lot.
While some may be quick to jump to the conclusion that it was a damaged battery pack that caused the fire, there is still no official word on the cause. However, this is not the first Rivian vehicle fire reported. In July, several Rivian vans built for Amazon burned at an Amazon center in Houston, Texas. Rivian asserted that the high-voltage batteries were not the root cause of that fire.
Electric vehicle fires are rare but when they do occur, they can be more difficult to extinguish compared to gasoline fires.
The Rivian factory in Normal, Illinois currently manufactures the R1T and R1S models. Back in May, Rivian received over $800 million in state funding to expand the plant to manufacture their new midsize SUV model, the R2. Since 2021 Rivian has built over 100,000 EVs at this facility.

Rivian Travel Kitchen Was Literally Recalled During Shipping , Reason Unknown
documents.text:
We're used to seeing fierce debates every time a recall is announced, especially if it's Tesla and the fix is a software update. However, Rivian might be the company that initiated the weirdest recall in recent history. Strangely, it affects the Travel Kitchen, an accessory that was supposed to replace another one that never shipped for equally mysterious reasons.
Rivian has an impeccable record of screwing up the features that could've become unique selling points for its electric vehicles. These included the powered tonneau cover (or any tonneau cover promised to replace it), the power outlets in the frunk, and now the Travel Kitchen.
The previous Camp Kitchen was praised by everyone who saw the concept, although the $6,000 price was scary. Maybe realizing that few people would've ordered one at that price, Rivian canceled it before anyone could order it. It promised to redesign the kitchen, and it came with the concept of a briefcase containing an induction cooker and pretty much nothing else, all for $1,400.
Few considered it compelling, especially as aftermarket solutions were better designed, sometimes for less money. This didn't prevent some from ordering one out of loyalty to the brand. However, after they got the message that their order had been shipped, they noticed that the package was not making progress. Upon trying to track it in the UPS systems, they learned that the Travel Kitchen had been recalled while in transit, and Rivian requested the return of the package.
Many have tried contacting Rivian for clarification, but they got mixed responses. Some were told that the package appeared as shipped in their system and didn't know about any request to return the package to the sender. Others were informed that "there is a delay in shipments," and Rivian aims to resume deliveries "in the near future" without further explanation of what caused said delay.
Nobody got a straight or satisfactory answer as to why the package had to make its way back to Rivian, sometimes after getting very close to the delivery address. Rivian also quietly stopped taking orders for the Travel Kitchen, now listed as "no stock" in the Gear Shop. So far, no one understands why Rivian withdrew it from the market, including items in transit to their customers. The EV startup is doing a poor job of explaining its actions, which is not working in its favor.
In the meantime, some lucky (or unlucky?) people have already got their hands on the Travel Kitchen and went camping to test it. The induction briefcase appears to function properly, although some complained of a leveling issue. Hardly the deal-breaking problems that would've caused a recall.

I've seen multiple reports of Rivian stopping UPS deliveries of the new Travel Kitchen and returning it to sender. In addition, the item is showing as "No Stock" on the store. Is there a recall underway for the new Travel Kitchen?… pic.twitter.com/jxRMHw47kD

Rivian Factory Fire : Rivian Either Has Outstanding Quality Control or Is Extremely Lucky
documents.text:
EV fires are frightening events with a high emotional charge precisely because they seldom happen. Statistics show EVs are 60 times less likely to catch fire than gas-powered vehicles. NTSB data shows that only 25 fires have been recorded for every 100,000 EVs sold, compared to 1,530 for every 100,000 gas-powered vehicles sold. However, whenever a fire and an electric vehicle share the same informational space, people get the impression that EVs are time bombs that can blow off at any minute.
This was again brought into the spotlight on Saturday night when a fire erupted at Rivian's plant in Normal, Illinois. So far, the cause of the fire is unknown, although we know that it started from a vehicle stored in a parking lot at the factory. Thankfully, no person was injured, and the Normal firefighters extinguished the fire in a couple of hours.
People who work at Rivian's factory (or have friends working there) explained on Reddit that the fire appeared to have originated in a vehicle stored in a parking lot reserved for vehicles that need repairs. If this is true, it looks like Rivian has some killer quality control, being able to single out these defective vehicles before they were shipped to customers. This is all the more impressive, considering that we haven't found out about fires on Rivian vehicles already shipped to customers.
Unfortunately, the fire spread rapidly, destroying over 50 vehicles. It's unclear what caused the fire, with Rivian and the Normal, Il, fire department working to discover what went wrong. The fact that the fire was extinguished in about two hours suggests that the battery packs were not involved this time. Li-ion battery fires are notoriously difficult to put out, and most of the time, firefighters let them burn until the chemical substances that maintain fire are exhausted.
Pictures taken from a drone in the aftermath of the fire show dozens of charred vehicles in an area surrounded by shipping containers and fences. These were undoubtedly installed to prevent the fire from spreading to other areas of the outbound lot. While some people claimed that the fire started on the railroad next to the lot, there are no burn signs near the rail tracks, except in the affected parking lot.
This is not the first fire at Rivian's factory, which has been in the news more than other car factories in the past years. Although we don't have a definitive statistic, we've tracked Rivian fires since the EV startup shipped its first pickups in 2021. Some of the fires have been caused by Li-ion battery packs, but others had more common causes. Whatever the reason, the Normal Fire Department must have become an expert in dealing with battery and EV fires by now.

documents.title: Empirical Test Shows How Much Solar Protection Rivian Dynamic Glass Roof Offers
documents.text:
A week ago, Rivian fans discussed the benefits of the so-called Dynamic Glass Roof that Rivian is now offering on select Gen 2 vehicles. This costs $1,500 on Adventure models and is included free of charge with the Ascend package. It's unavailable on the Dual Motor with Standard battery pack, though, so you'll have to upgrade to the Large pack to add it to your configuration.
It was impossible to reach a conclusion because not all people are the same, and they live in various climates. Some have hailed the Dynamic Glass Roof as a great tool to keep the cabin cooler when parked in the sun. Others, on the contrary, only see the Dynamic Glass Roof as offering privacy and little (if any) solar protection. The latter group got on the same side of the fence with Rivian, which played it safe and said that Dynamic Glass doesn't provide any UV or temperature-related benefits over the standard glass roof.
However, not everyone wanted to rely on official information, so they thought of doing a test on their own. One Rivian R1S (Gen 2) owner bought a solar energy meter and proceeded to measure the light intensity (in watts per square meter) at various points with and without the electrochromic layer activated. While this can't offer a definitive answer regarding UV or heat protection, it can still provide a clue about how much of the sun rays the Dynamic Glass Roof can block.
The tests were done in the Bay Area around 3 PM local time, at an outside temperature of 83 degrees. The R1S had no window tints, which was perfect for this assessment. The results were rather surprising, although they showed that the Dynamic Glass offers better protection than the regular glass roof. Specifically, DGR let about 14 W/sqm when transparent and 10.8 W/sqm when opaque. This compares favorably to the regular panoramic glass roof, which let in 28.7 W/sqm.
However different, both types of glass do a decent job at blocking sun rays. To put things into perspective, the windshield lets in 506.3 W/sqm, while the front side windows, 400.3 W/sqm. Rear passenger windows offer better protection at 116 W/sqm. This shows that applying UV protection film on the panoramic roof is a waste of money. You better use it on tinting the front windows, and make sure to use IR protection to reduce the heat inside the cabin during those hot summer days.

documents.title: Rivian EVs are Damaged as Illinois Factory Suffers Fire Incident
documents.text:
A fire broke out at Rivian's Normal, Illinois factory last Saturday night and it led to some of its electric vehicles (EVs) suffering from damages as a result of the incident. The fire remains under investigation by authorities.
It has been reported that the fire started in the factory's parking lot and were contained there.
Rivian's Illinois Factory Sees Damages to EVs
The Verge reported
that a fire broke out that authorities are still in the midst of investigating what caused the fire inn the parking lot. It has not been confirmed as of press time if the EVs themselves were the cause of the fire that broke out.
As previously mentioned, some of the EVs stationed at the parking lot sustained damages due to the fire. Rivian, as of press time, has yet to confirm the extent of both the fire and the damages incurred by its vehicles.
EV fires are massive hazards, especially for people who find themselve trapped inside during the fire. This is due to the lithium-ion (Li-On) batteries that can burn to extreme temperatures. These batteries are likewise difficult to extinguish using traditional methods.
More firefighters are now being trained to handle EV fires as these vehicles are becoming more common on the streets, particularly with the United States government's campaign towards the use of clean-energy vehicles.
Assembly Plant is 'Unaffected' by Rivian Fire Incident
It was also revealed by the local fire department and Rivian's spokesperson that the Illinois assembly plant of the EV company was "unaffected" by the recent blazing incident. It is an isolated case in the parking lot, and this may mean that operations will continue this week.
Moreover, there were no injuries or casualties caused by the Rivian factory fire, to both its employees and the firefighters who responded on the scene.
Electric Vehicle Fires Can Also Happen
It typically makes more sense for Internal combustion engine (ICE) cars to catch fire due to the presence of fuel and combustions. However, EVs are not exempted from such problems as well, especially during accidents. Not only can electrical wirings trigger fires, but there are also the highly flammable Li-On batteries that power everything in the vehicle.
However, these EV batteries are sealed and equipped with the right protection to avoid such incidents. That being said, accidents like crashes can cause a wide variety of hazards, as well as starting fires among electric vehicles.
Such problems are not limited to Rivian EVs. Tesla EVs, for example, have had its fair share of incidents and accidents. One incident involved its Model S "spontaneously combusted" in Sacramento last year, and the incident ended up closing down a part of EB Highway 50.
There were also previous incidents of overheating batteries that could cause it to catch fire. It can be recalled that GM's Chevrolet Bolt EV was previously recalled to avoid this. .

After Blaze in Rivian Parking Lot , Local Fire Dept Does Some EV Fire Myth - Busting
documents.text:
After a fire broke out at a Rivian plant over the weekend, the local fire department is taking the opportunity to dispel myths about electric vehicle fires.
"There are many rumors that EV fires cannot be extinguished, or that we have to use specialized chemicals or foam to extinguish them, and that simply isn't true," Matt Swaney, public information officer for the Normal Fire Department in Illinois, tells PCMag.
The cause of the incident is still under investigation, which is being conducted by a team of Rivian engineers and fire investigators. What we know now is that an unknown number of vehicles awaiting delivery caught fire in a parking lot, creating a large plume of smoke that was spotted by community members, according to local media reports. No one was harmed during the incident, and the plant itself was not damaged.
EVs have developed a reputation for taking more water and more time to extinguish than gas-powered vehicles. A UK-based fire crew estimated that EV fires take four to five hours to put out, as opposed to 30 minutes for a typical gas-powered car, the BBC reported in March.
Swaney didn't say how long it took to put out the blaze or how much water was required. Instead, he emphasized that putting out the flames was a routine process similar to what they do for an internal combustion fire. When the battery begins burning, it causes a chain reaction that can be "difficult to stop," he says, but water is enough to cool it, slowing and ultimately stopping the reaction.
"Being the home town of an EV manufacturer, we have had the opportunity to learn first hand the best practices when extinguishing EV fires," Swaney says.
Fire departments around the world are adapting to the growing number of EVs on the road, and updating their procedures to combat them. A Maryland crew has found success using fire blankets and specialized hose nozzles, NBC Washington reports. The International Association of Fire Chiefs maintains a comprehensive guide for putting out EV fires, with instructions for before, during, and after the incident.
Swaney blames sensational headlines for creating a false image of EVs as being exceptionally dangerous, and notes that combustion vehicle fires "happen every day and far more than most people realize." Gas-powered vehicles have more hazards due to the various oils, fluids, and, of course, gas, which EVs don't have, he says.
EVs are involved in approximately 25 fires for every 100,000 vehicles sold, according to National Transportation Safety Board data compiled by AutoinsuranceEZ. That's compared to 1,530 gasoline-powered vehicles and 3,475 hybrid vehicles for every 100,000 sold.

documents.title: Rivian Tests New Software Update With Navigation and Climate Control Improvements
documents.text:
Software updates have been the bread and butter at Rivian, which bet much of its success on a comprehensive software experience. The EV startup insists that its software provides better features than smartphone projection systems like Android Auto and Apple CarPlay, which have been insistently requested by its user base. This comes with high expectations, so Rivian is busy trying to accommodate as many features as possible.
While matching Apple CarPlay and Android Auto in features might not be possible anytime soon, it's not for the lack of trying. Rivian has been among the most active carmakers on the software front, with new features launched regularly. The EV startup usually rolls out monthly updates, most of which are feature-packed. As soon as they are deployed to customer vehicles, Rivian software engineers already start testing the next software update.
Earlier this month, Rivian began testing the 2024.27 software updates, with its 2024.27.01 and 2024.27.30 variants tailored for Gen 1 and Gen 2 vehicles, respectively. The update included adaptive LED matrix lights, native Apple Music and Audible apps, alongside a 60-day Connect+ free trial. On August 18, these updates were pushed to customer vehicles. Not everything was perfect, and some owners complained about lost internet connection, Apple Music bugs, or not being able to install the update at all.
Hopefully, the upcoming update, which the Rivian software team started working on immediately, will show better quality control. A little earlier than expected, Rivian already started internal testing the 2024.31 software update. This hopefully leaves the team more time to iron out all the bugs before rolling it out to customers.
The update differs slightly for the two crops of R1 vehicles, as was the case with previous updates. While both R1 generations get navigation improvements and an enhanced Auto mode for cabin climate, Gen 1 vehicles get color themes for accent lighting. These are already included with Gen 2 vehicles, which explains the difference. As a bonus, Gen 2 tri-motor models receive a new Launch Mode designed for use on a close-circuit track. The mode provides increased acceleration and top speed while also offering critical stats during and after the run.
Besides many bug fixes and improvements, the 2024.31 update introduced a lower limit for the Pet Comfort temperature setting to 63 F (17 C). This feature was requested by Kyle Conner from Out of Spec Studios, as stated in the update's release notes. It's not the only climate-related improvement. Both R1 generations get Low, Medium, and High settings for the Auto climate mode. Now, if you change the fan speed, the climate system will remain in Auto mode to keep the cabin climate comfortable.

Rivian Now Has a Referral Program , Start Calling Your Friends and Family [ UPDATED ]
documents.text:
Back when Tesla was trying to convince people that zero-tailpipe emission mobility was the next best thing, it tried something incredibly courageous. The hopeful startup incentivized early adopters to show off their rides and convince their friends to join them in becoming Tesla owners.
The program was popular, and it worked quite well. Many bought a Model S and discovered that a battery-electric vehicle, although expensive, didn't necessarily lead to a dramatic lifestyle change.
The disappointing aspect of the world's most valuable automaker's referral program is that it promised some people free Tesla Roadsters. That happened five years ago, and we're now at a point where the company's CEO promises that the open-top high-performance ride can fly even though it's nowhere to be seen, not even in prototype form.
But alas, Tesla's Tesla. The same executive also said that the Cybertruck, which has peelable trim, could briefly act as a boat and cross calm seas.
Fortunately, overpromising and underdelivering isn't Rivian's mantra – for now. We'll see how the brand evolves as it tries to reach profitability. There are no guarantees in life, especially when for-profit companies are involved.
However, existing and prospective Rivian owners have something new to be excited about. The referral program is now live, and it helps everyone involved feel a little bit more appreciated for choosing one of the Irvine-based manufacturer's pricey EVs.
For each friend, coworker, or family member who buys a Rivian with your unique referral code, you will receive six months of free charging with the marque's own high-power charging network, known as the Rivian Adventure Network. The perk is automatically applied when you stop at a Rivian dispenser for some electrons.
The bonuses will be awarded in about a fortnight after the referee takes delivery of their new whip.
The best thing about this whole initiative is that the referee gets the same rewards as the referrer. Everyone wins, and there won't be any animosity between the two of you because the benefits are the same.
The only thing you, as the referrer, need to be aware of is that the DC charging perk can only be stacked for a maximum of 36 months (three years). It doesn't matter if six or 60 people buy a Rivian with your unique code; you're still getting only 36 months of free battery replenishing sessions.
Also, make sure to use your rewards. They expire 24 months (two years) after being added to your Rivian account.
IMPORTANT. Make sure to tell your friends that the referral code must be added at checkout. They will not be able to add it after the order has already been placed! For now, the automaker does not offer an option to add the code after the order has been sent.
Finally, the young marque will take 100 Rivian owners who make 25 successful referrals to a special weekend event in 2025. The details aren't known yet, but the company does know how to make its customers feel special and appreciated.

documents.title: Rivian Automotive ( NASDAQ : RIVN ) Shares Down 1 . 3 %
Ford Ditches Its Electric SUV : Here What That Means For Rivian Stock
documents.text:
Shifting winds have hit the automotive market. After years of unit growth for battery-powered electric vehicles (EVs), the sector has begun to stagnate. New unit sales for EVs were growing 51% year over year less than a year ago. In the first quarter of 2024, that growth rate collapsed to zero, meaning the number of EVs sold in the United States was the same as a year ago.
What is replacing this growth? Plug-in hybrids. The versatile technology that brings battery charging and gasoline-powered engines to the same vehicle is growing north of 50% year over year, making up the majority of growth for the automotive market in 2024. This has inspired Ford (F +2.17%) to scrap plans for an all-electric SUV, replacing the upcoming model with a plug-in hybrid.
Does this spell trouble for full EV upstarts such as Rivian Automotive (RIVN +0.48%), a company betting on all-electric pick-up trucks and SUVs? Let's investigate further and find out.
Ford's changing product strategy
A few years ago, Ford began investing heavily in battery power and EV technologies. It came out with the Mustang Mach-E and F-150 Lightning. In 2021, it announced an $11.4 billion investment into new American factories set to pump out batteries and electric cars. Now, it has announced a pivot to this strategy.
Instead of a fully electric vehicle, Ford's upcoming SUV models will be plug-in hybrids. This doesn't mean Ford's $11.4 billion investment will go completely to waste, as these vehicles still require sizable lithium-ion batteries. They just don't need nearly the amount of raw materials for the batteries, which saves on costs. People are saying they want the flexibility of a plug-in hybrid as well. While full EVs are not growing in the United States, plug-in hybrid sales jumped 59% year over year in Q1 2024.
For right now at least, people want the flexibility of a plug-in hybrid over the fully electric vehicles produced by the likes of Rivian or Tesla. But what does it mean for these businesses?
NASDAQ: RIVN
Key Data Points
A double-edged sword for Rivian
On the one hand, investors could argue that Rivian is on the right side of history. The company produces all-electric SUVs and pick-up trucks. People are now saying they want more environmentally friendly cars to drive, and that eventually traditional full internal combustion vehicles will go extinct.
The problem is, Rivian has limited itself to not selling plug-in hybrids, which is where all the growth is today. You can see it in its delivery and production figures. Rivian's production has not grown over the last few quarters and seems stuck at around 60,000 vehicles a year. Deliveries have climbed slightly, but that is due to Rivian selling through some inventory that built up in late 2023. The trailing rate of deliveries has only just caught up to the trailing rate of production.
This growth slowdown coincides perfectly with the uptick in plug-in hybrid sales. The problem is that -- especially with larger vehicles like SUVs and pick-up trucks -- you need extra-large batteries. Larger batteries mean higher input costs, which consumers are not willing to pay up for. Even though the average Rivian pick-up truck starts at $75,000, the company has a shocking negative 41% gross margin.
Is Rivian stock a buy?
An automotive market trending to plug-in hybrids is a disastrous development for Rivian. The company needs customers willing to pay up for premium EVs, and to reach a larger production scale to bring its gross margins from negative to positive. This is what happened to Tesla when it ramped up Model 3 production, for reference.
Bringing a completely new car model to market costs billions of dollars. From design to supply chain procurement to capital investments in the manufacturing plants, there is no way to shortcut the automotive production process. Rivian is burning $5 billion a year and has less than $8 billion in cash on the balance sheet. It likely does not have the time or the money to invest in a plug-in hybrid unless it can secure billions more in financing from outside investors.
Up until late last year, Rivian's gross margin was moving in the right direction. It still had a long ways to go, but you had a line of sight to improvement and eventual profits as the company scaled up production. Now, gross margins have stagnated at well in the negative territory, along with production and deliveries to customers. This coincided with the growth in demand for plug-in hybrids in the United States.
If the growth in plug-in hybrids continues, Rivian's business will continue to struggle. From my seat, this means investors should avoid buying this risky and unprofitable stock at the moment.

documents.title: Tesla CEO Elon Musk Doubts Volkswagen Proposed $5B Rivian Investment Amid Reports That It Is Considering Closing Its Factories In Germany :  Where Will They Get The Money ? - Volkswagen ( OTC : VWAGY ), Rivian Automotive ( NASDAQ : RIVN )
documents.text:
Tesla Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA) CEO Elon Musk on Monday raised doubts about California-based EV startup Rivian Automotive (NASDAQ:RIVN) getting money from German automaker Volkswagen as part of a recently announced joint venture.
What Happened: “Where will they get the money?,” Musk wrote on X in response to a Tesla enthusiast who mocked Rivian for banking on Volkswagen for funding when the German automaker itself is shutting down factories in Germany.
The Tesla enthusiast also predicted “major drama” going forward for Volkswagen as unions might resist the company giving money to an American startup while there are job cuts at home.
Musk’s comments come on the heels of reports that the German automaker is considering closing factories in Germany for the first time in its 87-year history.
The company is now considering closing vehicle production and component factories in a bid to cut costs amid fierce competition, reported the New York Times. IG Metall union, which represents automotive workers, has said that they will resist job cuts.
Union leaders and workers’ representatives hold half the seats on Volkswagen’s supervisory board.
Why It Matters: Rivian announced its intent to form an equally owned JV with German automaker Volkswagen in June. As part of the deal, Volkswagen has made a $1 billion initial investment in Rivian and will make additional investments of up to $4 billion subject to certain conditions for a total deal size of $5 billion. The JV is aimed at the creation of next-generation software-defined vehicle platforms to be used in both companies' future EVs.
"Assuming all criteria are met, we expect that the full $5 billion is intended to flow to the benefit of Rivian," company CFO Claire McDonough said last month at the company’s second-quarter earnings call. "In addition to the $5 billion of capital to Rivian, we anticipate incremental benefits through cost savings on materials, operating expense efficiencies, and future revenue opportunities associated with the joint venture."
The additional liquidity provided by the deal, the CFO said, will allow the company to ramp production of its R2 SUV at its facility in Normal, Illinois, and enable a path to positive cash flow. Rivian intends to launch the R2 in the first half of 2026.
Rivian ended the second quarter of 2024 with $7.87 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments.
Volkswagen did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comment on the impact of the proposed shutdowns on its planned investment into Rivian. A Rivian spokesperson refused to comment.

documents.text:
Electric vehicle manufacturer Rivian seeks lease for Woodbury warehouse in pitch to Oyster Bay
A Woodbury warehouse owner has pitched the Town of Oyster Bay on a plan to lease part of its 9-acre property to Rivian, the electric vehicle manufacturer.
The Woodbury facility would become Rivian's first permanent service center on Long Island. The company would use 41,000 square feet of the warehouse to service vehicles. It will also store vehicles that customers have ordered online and had shipped to the center. The facility previously housed News 12 studios.
"We’ve redeveloped the site as a 145,000-square-foot warehouse," Philip Butler, an attorney representing Rockefeller Group, which owns the property, told Oyster Bay officials at a board meeting last month. Since finishing the renovation, the group has been searching for a new occupant, Butler said. "We are currently in discussions with Rivian."
The earliest the town can vote on the proposal is during its October meeting, said Marta Kane, a spokeswoman for Oyster Bay.
Rivian, founded in 2009, has three vehicle models: a commercial van, a pickup truck and a three-row SUV, but plans to expand its vehicle line. The pickup truck starts around $70,000, while the SUV starts at about $76,000, according to its website.
By the end of 2026, the company expects to add two more models at a lower price range, said Dan Vitale, who represented Rivian at the August board meeting.
For battery replacement repairs, Vitale said batteries are shipped from a factory to a service facility and remain at the location for a maximum of 72 hours. Batteries are otherwise not stored on site, he said.
Rivian previously had an exclusive deal with Amazon that provided the delivery giant with commercial vans, but the manufacturer in 2023 said it would allow other companies to buy the delivery vehicles.
Rivian shares surged sharply in late June after Volkswagen vowed to invest $1 billion in the company. Currently, the electric car manufacturer’s website indicates there are no service centers on Long Island, with the nearest facility in Brooklyn.
Greg Rakovsky, 40, of Oceanside, is on a waiting list for a Rivian vehicle. But he said the lack of a Long Island service center gives him pause.
"Right now, it would be a drive to downtown Brooklyn," Rakovsky said in an interview. "I think it’s critical for them to open on Long Island because there’s a pretty big market. I’m seeing two, three, four Rivians per day now."
There were nearly 65,000 electric vehicles on the road on Long Island as of Aug. 2, according to the New York State Energy Research and Development Authority. Tesla vehicles comprise the vast majority of that total, which included about 620 Rivian passenger vehicles.
The company's push for a lower price point — and a Long Island service center — should expand that total over time, said Rosemary Mascali, a chairwoman for the Drive Electric Long Island Coalition, a nonprofit advocacy group. Having a Long Island service facility should boost Rivian sales on Long Island.
"If you're going to buy a car from a manufacturer, I think it's an important element to know where you're going to service it," Mascali said. "And if the closest is in Brooklyn, I think that would be a blocking factor to people."

Software Bug Allows Accessing of R1S Large+ Full Battery Capacity , Rivian Unhappy
documents.text:
Rivian is streamlining its battery pack options for the Gen 2 R1 vehicles for the first time. The refreshed R1 lineup was officially listed with three battery options: Standard (92.5 kWh, LFP), Large (109.4 kWh, NMC), and Max (141.5 kWh, NMC). However, people discovered last month that Rivian quietly launched a new battery option called Large+ (or Large Plus, as listed in the vehicle's infotainment system).
Rivian confirmed that the Large+ pack was a Max battery that is software-capped to 120 kWh. This presents a few advantages for Rivian owners while allowing the EV startup to simplify logistics and manufacturing. Besides having a larger capacity than the Large pack, the Large+ pack can be charged to 100% without causing accelerated wear, which is an important benefit. Also, for the people who tow, the Large+ pack offers the improved towing capacity of the Max pack.
Since charging the Large+ pack to 100% would not, in theory, affect the battery's lifecycle, some owners did use this feature. However, as they did, they discovered that the battery continued charging even beyond the 100% limit. This was not shown in the infotainment system, as the Rivian R1 vehicles don't show a state of charge higher than 100%.
However, according to one report, the battery needed an hour to charge from 99% to 100%. While the car's computer still shows the Large+ range, driving will not cause the range to drop. Another R1S owner wrote on X that he drove about 31 miles without causing the range to drop from 329 miles or the state of charge to fall below 99%. This suggests that the vehicle treats the battery as an unlocked Max pack, allowing the battery to fully charge. However, it doesn't know enough to show the real range on the vehicle's screen.
As owners suspected a software bug causing this, they contacted Rivian, which confirmed this was a calibration problem. Rivian apparently rushed the Large+ packs to the market to meet demand, and some details have been overlooked. However, you don't have to be upset because Rivian knows and is already offering a fix with the 2024.31.30 software update.
I suspect some Rivian owners would want to defer the update to enjoy the Max pack capacity at Large+ price. However, refusing an update is not a solution. Even if you could, you'd be missing out on important features and bug fixes. The 2024.31.30 update, for instance, brings improvements to the navigation search experience, enhanced Auto mode for cabin climate, and a new launch mode for tri-motor vehicles.
Over the weekend we completed a 0-100% charging session of our new 2nd gen R1S Large+ (software limited Max ) R1S to learn more about the charge curve.
While we were unable to get a full power session, after an hour it hit 99% SOC… and it just kept charging!
A full hour later… pic.twitter.com/KF7Yr25yPp

documents.title: Rivian Automotive ( NASDAQ : RIVN ) Shares Down 3 . 7 %
Rivian moves toward expansion across the street in Normal
Rivian : Buy , Sell , or Hold ?
This Wall Street Pro Thinks Rivian Stock Has 42 % Upside
documents.text:
Wall Street doesn't know what to make of Rivian (RIVN +0.48%) stock. Price targets range from $14 to $19 per share. With the stock price currently hovering around $13, there's either minimal near-term upside or plenty of it. So which is it? One analyst recently reaffirmed his outperform rating for Rivian, reiterating confidence in his $19 price target with 42% in expected upside, the most bullish outlook on Wall Street.
Could there really by 42% upside to Rivian stock over the next 12 months? There's reason to believe this analyst could be right.
NASDAQ: RIVN
Key Data Points
Expect this from Rivian over the next 12 months
Predicting the short-term direction of a stock can be difficult. But predicting what will happen from a business standpoint is much more manageable. That's especially true for a company like Rivian, for which the events of the next several years are predictable.
First, let's recap Rivian's current predicament. On paper, the company has done extraordinarily well recently. In a few short years, it went from almost zero revenue to more than $5 billion. It achieved this because of just two models: the R1T and R1S, both luxury vehicles aimed at the upper end of the market. In many ways, Rivian's beginning mirrors that of Tesla, which first hit the market with high-priced models meant mostly to establish a reputation for quality and execution.
Rivian should also do what Tesla did next. After the success of its Model S and Model X variants, Tesla then leveraged its newfound reputation and access to capital to hit the mass market with its Model 3 and Model Y variants. This transition increased revenue from around Rivian's current level to nearly $100 billion. Rivian expects to replicate this rise with its recently announced R2, R3, and R3X models, all of which are expected to debut under $50,000. These models should dramatically expand Rivian's addressable market, with revenues rising rapidly in response.
Rivian's new models won't hit the road until the first half of 2026. So the year ahead will be fairly quiet, filled mostly with updates to manufacturing capacities and production timelines. But one event in the next 12 months could be a huge catalyst for the stock. It's what has Wall Street's most bullish analyst so optimistic.
This catalyst could add fuel to this EV stock
A major difference between Tesla and Rivian right now is their respective abilities to generate positive gross margins. Tesla is turning a profit for each vehicle it sells and has done so for years. As a smaller competitor, meanwhile, Rivian is still losing tens of thousands of dollars for every vehicle it sells. But management expects this to change fairly soon. Last month, Rivian executives confirmed that they expect to reach positive gross margins by the fourth quarter of 2024. Over the past year, Rivian has trimmed its gross loss per vehicle to just $6,000 from $33,000. Erasing the final deficit would lend credibility to management and their ability to prudently manage its finances as the company ramps up spending to support its new mass-market models.
Canaccord analyst George Gianarikas believes this flip to profitability will prove to the market that Rivian is not "one of the EV walking dead," giving the company enough momentum to reach its R2, R3, and R3X sales launch. This boost, he argues, will help Rivian "push through, shake off operational cobwebs, and breathe life into its mass market lineup -- the R2/R3; and achieve scale."
If Rivian can achieve positive gross margins this year, its outlook for 2025 and beyond will improve considerably. And when its mass-market vehicles hit the road, the company's current $13 billion valuation may end up looking like a steal. But investors will need to be patient to see this story through.

Wolfe Research Begins Coverage on Rivian Automotive ( NASDAQ : RIVN )
Why Rivian And VW Both Need Each Other
Rivian Will Offer Self - Driving Software Subscriptions , Use VW Money for the R2 : CFO
documents.text:
The executive attended Goldman Sachs' Communacopia + Technology conference and answered a few questions that allow existing and prospective investors to better understand where Rivian is heading.
She explained that the automaker's goal from the very beginning (after it had decided that it wouldn't make plug-in hybrids) was not to produce the best electric vehicle (EV) but the best vehicle on the market. That's how it all started, and that's the main reason why the R1T with four Bosch motors was so capable from the start. It was overengineered solely to make a statement.
However, behind the curtains, things aren't going that great. McDonough explained that Rivian is going through supply challenges and had to temporarily stop the production of EDVs. Apparently, parts are a bit scarce and hard to source at a fair price. However, that's supposedly on Rivian because it only asks for "upscale" parts. It doesn't want to compromise, which is understandable since its most affordable whip costs $72,000 with shipping and handling.
But the automaker won't give up now. It's currently trying to create more awareness for its brand via the so-called "Spaces" that serve as showrooms and more service centers where people can test-drive its EVs or take delivery. Increasing sales of R1-series EVs completes the strategy for a more prominent physical presence.
Rivian's plans for the immediate future
Currently, the EV maker is in the midst of finalizing the deal with Volkswagen. It should happen before Thanksgiving.
Rivian could unlock more potential for VW's future vehicles because they'll work together on refining the most important tidbits. Electric hardware and software from Rivian will be infused into upcoming zero-tailpipe emission VWs. Rivian's ethos could soon be applied to hundreds of thousands of vehicles, which will only help refine the technology used by both companies. The only difference? The interface. That's mostly what this deal is all about.
But probably the most important thing about the joint venture with Volkswagen is that Rivian won't have to spend money on making something work for itself and its customers. Per the CFO, the partnership with VW will also result in sharing future development costs.
Next year, the Irvine-based brand with a factory in Normal, Illinois, plans to temporarily close up shop again. In the second half of 2025, some downtime will be needed to integrate the R2 on the production line.
Rivian still plans to sell EDVs to other customers that aren't Amazon. It's currently running pilot programs with some "big names," but the executive wasn't willing to say who exactly is trying out the EDV and the associated software. Per McDonough, they're still at an educational point. They're discussing things like buying costs versus operational expenditures. Prospective customers don't appear too convinced about a higher initial cost.
However, Rivian may not be very confident about its van program. It plans to have only one shift for the EDV in 2025. Still, the CFO said that workers would be moved from one production line to another so Rivian wouldn't have to spend more on the workforce or deal with complicated scheduling.
Rivian appears to anticipate an increase in demand because it publicly said that it wants its suppliers to keep up with its requests. The brand wants its partners to invest more in their capabilities before it starts signing demanding contracts with them.
Sadly, subscriptions are unavoidable
"Autonomy creates a large-scale opportunity because customers can pay for features directly via the infotainment screen," said McDonough.
Rivian is likely going to launch "pay-to-play" autonomy features in 2025, which will probably be made available to Gen 2 R1-series first because they have better hardware. The Autonomy+ platform is still young but might be key to Rivian's profitability. Fret not; Rivian's isn't betting the house on solving autonomous driving, and it isn't promising robotaxis. The company is still making money off environmental credits it sells to other brands.
Interestingly, the executive said that self-driving tech is based on an AI-first approach, which means that Rivian EVs on the road today are helping the company improve its self-driving software. We might see things take a turn for the better once the VW money starts pouring in, and Rivian can spend more on computing power. It could also share the financial burden with the Germans!
Moreover, the CFO expects Rivian Gen 2 R1-series EVs to help it become profitable because the quad-motor will join the offering as the portfolio's pinnacle. Rivian doesn't appear to target profitability this year anymore.
However, the CFO said that she expects positive earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) in 2027. The target is based on Rivian selling 200,000 EVs in a full fiscal year. EBITDA is used to measure a company's operating performance or indicate its ability to generate consistent profit.
R2, VW, Germany, and Europe
The CFO said that the R2 development is going well, but didn't expand. She only reminded everyone that the supply chain is a bit complicated to deal with at the moment. Demand and consumer enthusiasm for R2 (and R3 and R3X) encourage the company to push forward, though!
Post-2025, Rivian wants to use Germany as the entry point to Europe. It'll take advantage of the already established EDV network to start selling the R2. However, R1S' shorter sibling will be sold in Europe only after it makes a splash in North America. The Old Continent isn't a priority.
Europeans don't have to be sad. They might end up winners because Rivian could work out any possible shortcomings before exporting the R2 to the right side of the pond.
However, McDonough wants everyone to keep in mind that R2 is designed for a global market. So, the brand could target certain parts of Africa, Asia, and Australia, too. After all, multiple R1Ts are already in Africa and the land down under.
The CFO also said that Gen 1 to Gen 2 trade-ins should be made easier soon and underlined that NACS adapters will be sent to more customers sooner rather than later.
A couple of more insights
McDonough answered some questions from participants. Most notably, she said that range anxiety remains a key constraint to EV adoption, but reliable DC fast-charging infrastructure could help alleviate those worries. She said that reliable charging networks are paramount to enable EV owners to travel across the country comfortably, and that's why the brand invests in the Rivian Adventure Network (RAN). Increasing battery pack sizes doesn't make too much sense from a weight and cost perspective. We'd argue that it also isn't a good thing for green credentials, which is something many automakers appear to have forgotten.
Rivian's CFO also believes that EVs must become more affordable. They should be on par with gas-powered equivalents and make more sense for the consumer.
McDonough also confirmed that Rivian isn't afraid of Chinese EVs, even though they are generally more affordable and can have better tech. Rivian has the advantage of being known for enabling drivers to go with their R1-series ride almost wherever they want. Rivian also targets customers who buy "nice" traditional vehicles, not those looking to maximize dollar value.
Last year, Rivian's CFO attended the same event and gave us a few important hints regarding the evolution of the R1-series EVs and the company's direction. That's when we learned about the simplified R1 architecture, the smart cost-reduction process, the R2 going to Europe (at some point), and the addition of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries for the R1T and R1S. McDonough also confirmed that Rivian would charge for premium software features, which it has just started to do via Connect+. Thus, the executive's participation at Communacopia 2024 should help Rivian assure investors that it's on the right track and convince customers that a Fisker-like fiasco is downright impossible.
Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe will discuss the company's future at a Morgan Stanley conference on Wednesday. We will bring you the most important details from that meeting, too.

documents.title: Why Rivian Stock Fell 14 % in August After a Massive Rally
documents.text:
Rivian Automotive (RIVN +0.48%) stock gained a staggering 84% in the three months between May and July. That seemingly unstoppable rally ground to a halt last month, with the electric vehicle (EV) stock losing 13.9% of its value in August, according to data provided by S&P Global Market Intelligence. Rivian shares remain under pressure and are down another 4% this month, as of this writing.
What's going on with Rivian stock?
Rivian continues to incur big losses
Rivian announced its second-quarter numbers in August, and they looked promising. Rivian's Q2 deliveries jumped 9% year over year to 13,790 units, generating roughly $1.2 billion in revenue. However, its production fell sharply, or by 31% year over year, to 9,612 vehicles. That drop in production shouldn't have come as a surprise, as Rivian had already announced a planned downtime in Q2 at its sole manufacturing plant in Illinois for a major retooling.
The retooling upgrade was important because Rivian expects much higher production efficiency and cost benefits going forward -- so much so that it is confident of achieving a positive gross profit in the fourth quarter. For perspective, Rivian generated a negative gross profit of $451 million in Q2. The plant is now also ready to ramp up production of EVs on Rivian's second-generation platform. Moreover, Rivian also reiterated its full-year production guidance of 57,000 units despite lower production in Q2.
So far, so good. Why then did Rivian shares fall in recent weeks? There are a couple of reasons.
NASDAQ: RIVN
Key Data Points
First, Rivian reported a bigger net loss, or nearly $1.5 billion in Q2 versus $1.2 billion in the year-ago quarter. Second, there were a few hiccups for the EV maker in August, such as a fire at its plant that damaged several EVs. A shortage of parts also forced Rivian to temporarily suspend production of its electric delivery vans (EDVs) for e-commerce leader Amazon last month. Rivian has an order to deliver 100,000 EDVs to Amazon through the end of this decade.
Should you buy Rivian stock now?
There's a lot going on at Rivian that's piqued investor interest in recent months. One of the biggest recent highlights has been Rivian's deal with Volkswagen, with the two companies planning to form a joint venture. Under the deal, Volkswagen made an initial investment of $1 billion in Rivian with plans to pump another $4 billion into it through 2026. The venture will likely focus on R2, Rivian's affordable SUV that should go into production in 2026.
In between, expectations of interest rate cuts have also sparked investor interest in Rivian shares as lower interest rates will make funding cheaper. Rivian is flush with cash for now, though, having ended the second quarter with nearly $7.9 billion in cash and equivalents and short-term investments.
Some market players perhaps took profits off the table last month after the stock's rally, but investor interest in Rivian will likely remain high as the company's gross margins improve and it starts production of R2 SUVs.

Rivian Finally Launches Referral Program , Offering $750 Credit And Free Charging
documents.text:
- Owners and buyers can receive up to six months of free charging at Rivian’s charging network.
- The first 100 owners making 25 referrals will receive an invite to a special “adventure weekend.”
- Rivian is following Tesla and Lucid, which have also launched their own referral programs.
Owners and buyers of Rivian vehicles are eligible to each receive a credit worth $750 thanks to the launch of a long-awaited referral program from the electric car manufacturer.
Tesla pioneered the concept of the referral program, encouraging its loyalists to recruit as many new buyers as possible using unique referral codes. In return, Tesla doled out discounts, credits, free charging, and other perks that fed into its cult-like following. Now, Rivian is clearly eyeing a similar path, but with a twist.
Rivian’s program offers a straightforward deal: 750 points (1 point equals a $1 credit) for an owner who makes a referral and another 750 points to a new buyer who uses that referral code. On top of this, both parties get six months of free charging at the Rivian Adventure Network, giving a little extra nudge for those on the fence.
Read: Over 50 Rivian R1T And R1S Models Ruined In Factory Fire
That $750 credit isn’t just a paper promise; it can be redeemed for a future vehicle purchase or spent on Rivian’s online store, which includes everything from branded apparel to vehicle accessories, according to Auto News. The first 100 owners who make 25 referrals will also be able to participate in a special “adventure weekend,” although the carmaker has yet to announce details about it.
Owners will only be able to redeem a maximum of three years’ worth of free charging through the referral program, but there doesn’t appear to be a cap on the number of credits they can receive. But remember, points earned will expire two years after they land in the owner’s account, so use them or lose them.
For now, the program is exclusively available to Rivian owners in the United States, but there are plans to expand to Canada next year, which should broaden its appeal.
“These programs appeal to automakers because they’re quite simple to implement and therefore less expensive to run compared to other advertising methods,” Edmunds analyst Ivan Drury explained.
“Creating a program where both parties receive benefits also creates a win-win situation, which likely encourages greater participation. As a lifestyle heavy product, Rivian offering points redeemable towards Rivian gear has twofold benefits: Many of the branded products serve as additional advertising, and the perceived value of the branded gear is likely higher than their actual cost to make,” he added.
